content: Every column `network_loader._route_record` emits must be present. Extra columns are allowed: exports from the raw zone carry the `year`/`month`/`day` partition keys.

Guards against a truncated Overpass response. Overpass sheds load by returning a partial body under HTTP 200, and `fetch_network` only rejects an *empty* one, so a short extract would otherwise flow through unnoticed. OSM had 515 route relations in the Quito bbox on 2026-08-19; a sudden collapse means a bad extract, not a city that lost its buses (docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md).
One row per OSM relation. Duplicates would also mean a batch has mixed two snapshots together, which defeats the row-count guard.
OSM relation ids, stored as strings. Catches a numeric round-trip that turns `85965` into `85965.0`, which would break every join in the warehouse.
Mirrors `OSM_ROUTE_TYPES` in ingestion/constants.py, which is also the filter in the Overpass query. Anything else means the query or the parser changed.
Community-mapped, so not strictly complete: 514 of 515 routes were named on 2026-08-19.

The README's claim of 93-99% completeness on `operator`, `ref`, `from` and `to` is what makes operator-coverage analysis sound. Below 90% that claim no longer holds and the analysis needs re-evaluating. Observed 2026-08-19: `route_ref` 94.2%, `operator` 93.6%, `origin` 93.6%, `destination` 93.6%.
ISO-8601 in UTC, as written by `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`. The staging models parse this string; a format change breaks them silently.

meta.description: Expectations for the raw OSM transit route relations (routes.parquet). Validates presence of the columns network_loader emits, null constraints on the identifier and on the tags the analysis depends on, the route-type vocabulary, and a minimum route count that guards against a truncated Overpass response. One of three suites covering the network snapshot: routes, stops and route_stops are separate tables with different columns, and a suite binds to one batch.
